assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

On 2.x the parent and its task-tool child are both sessions hosted by the one service; neither has a process of its own. Killing 'the parent's process' therefore means killing the service — the maintainer's Q1 window. With the child mid-tool, the service is SIGKILLed: the daemon's process watcher reports the service pid exited and HandleWatcherExit emits process_exited for every session bound to it, children first, deleting each with no state change (pid_manager.go). Children bind the service pid like any 2.x session (pid.go servicePIDFor falls back to the service with no parent check; Explore read, inferred for the child) — so the orphaned child is cleaned up by the same exit, and never transitions to working during it.

## Spec choices

- Parent working; a NEW child session linked to it.
- The kill lands while the child's shell tool runs (await_child, an observed condition), so no model request is in flight.
- process_exited for the child and for the parent; the child never goes working or waiting after cleanup.
caveats: Recorded only inside the approved service window: the sandbox service is SIGKILLed and the operator restores it right after (the PR body records old pid, new pid and the restore evidence).
The scenario's daemon-restart framing (#321) has no 2.x-specific path: the orphan is made by the host process dying, as V1's sigkill of `opencode run` made it.

sources.note: 2.x reader: lists session_v2 rows with time_archived IS NULL; a session is admitted on its first session_message activity while a service is up (#2107); an archived or missing row emits EventRemoved (v2SessionGone)
servicePIDFor: a session no client runs binds to the one running service; OwnsSharedPID answers false for an archived row

HandleProcessExit/HandleWatcherExit: every session bound to an exited pid gets process_exited and is deleted, children first; idlesOnHost lets the ready TTL reap an idle root on a live session host (opencode SessionHostArgv)
parent_linked is recorded from the child's ParentSessionID

preconditions: One OpenCode 2.x `serve --service` running, with a model it can reach (this host: the sandbox service, local Kolibri-1 4-bit model (mlx_lm) at 127.0.0.1:8087); the rig never starts or reconfigures it, and stops it only inside this cell's approved service window (OC2_SERVICE_WINDOW=1)
The three XDG exports, coexist IRRLICHT_ONBOARD_HOME and a non-7837 bind address from replaydata/agents/opencode-v2/prerequisites.md; OPENCODE_DB unset
setup: driver-interactive.sh (API driver) refuses before creating anything unless exactly one `serve --service` runs, its environment carries the run's XDG_* values, and the plugin's beacon resolves this run's daemon

It creates one session over POST /api/session at <staging>/cwd, waits for the service log to show the plugin the daemon installed loading for that location with no load failure, then drives the script; the session's session_message rows are exported read-only as the transcript

Service window (#2109 Q1, approved for 3-4 and for 1-2's service-exit variant only): the operator exports OC2_SERVICE_WINDOW=1, records the sandbox service's identity first, and restores it afterwards with the sandbox's own start command; the driver signals the service but never starts one
settings allow the shell tool in RUN_CWD/opencode.json, so the child's `sleep 30` runs without an ask

send; await_child until the child's shell tool runs; sigkill the service (every slot exported first); 15s. The prompt keeps the shell in the foreground: the first attempt's child set the shell tool's background:true, so the tool completed at once and was never seen running (the run timed out before any signal)

script.text: Use the task tool to launch a subagent (the built-in 'general' agent) that runs the shell command `sleep 30` in the FOREGROUND (the shell tool's background option must stay false) and then replies with exactly the word: finished. Wait for that subagent to finish, then reply with exactly the word: done.

verify: a child session linked to the parent
after the service's SIGKILL: process_exited for child and parent, no working transition for the orphan
